current_status.to: Extended via Ordinance 2026-14, adopted as an emergency measure at the 2026-07-06 Council meeting, imposing another 180-day moratorium (through approximately 2027-01-02); succeeds the original Ordinance 2025-13 (expired 2026-06-20). Active as of 2026-09-23; unaffected by the separate dispute below over the EdgeConneX development agreement. Separately, the underlying EdgeConneX development agreement (Resolution 06-2026, adopted 2026-04-06 as an emergency measure and exempted from the village's own data center moratorium) remains contested. The Ohio Supreme Court ruled 2026-08-07 (State ex rel. McNamara-Smith v. Grube) that Ashville's fiscal officer improperly refused to certify a citizen referendum petition against Resolution 06-2026 because the emergency declaration was not adequately justified; the Pickaway County Board of Elections then voted unanimously to place the referendum on the 2026-11-03 general-election ballot. Village Council subsequently introduced Resolution 16-2026 to repeal Resolution 06-2026 outright and moot the referendum; a 2026-09-08 motion to waive the second and third readings and pass it immediately fell short of the five-vote supermajority required (final tally of 4 in favor, after Mayor Clark broke an initial 3-3 tie, which the council's own rules held insufficient), and at the 2026-09-21 meeting Council instead advanced the repeal to a third reading scheduled for 2026-10-05. As of 2026-09-23, Resolution 06-2026 has not been repealed and the referendum remains scheduled for the November ballot.
